text: I must clarify that Multiple Sclerosis is not a diagnosis for an infant with these symptoms; your presentation of stridor, wheezing, and relief with neck extension is highly suggestive of a subglottic obstruction. Given the history of vomiting post-feeding and exacerbation with neck flexion, I am concerned about laryngomalacia versus a vascular ring or tracheomalacia. REQUEST IMAGES: Neck flexion and extension video fluoroscopy, and a CT Angiogram of the neck to rule out vascular compression.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with possible tracheomalacia. The classic symptoms of stridor worsening with crying and neck flexion, and improving with neck extension, combined with the normal workup so far, point to this upper airway disorder. I recommend a sleep study to assess for any associated obstructive sleep apnea before we proceed.
